title: Have Malaysian + Australian passport?
body:
O.P.
Hi, i was born in malaysia and obtained a citizenship by descent when i was 17 years of age as a parent is an australian citizen, i never renounced my Malaysian citizenship so i technically have a dual nationalities.
I previously had an 'Australian Declatory Visa' in my Malaysian passport, which is pretty much a visa that Australian citizens have that says they are unable to travel on an australian passport (because Malaysia doesnt allow dual citizenships), but i was flying from KUL-MEL once and the lady at at the check in seemed suspicious and had trouble 'clearing' me for the flight, check in took over 30 minutes with heaps of questions!
Anyway since then, i have been living in Oz for 3 years now, and i have obtained an Australian passport. I am travelling home soon for a quick visit/holiday, and i wanted to know which passport i should be using?
I called australian immigration and they advised to exit Oz on an Oz passport, and enter malaysia on a malaysian passport, and then exit malaysia on my malaysian passport and enter Oz with my Oz passport.
my main concerns with this is that upon entry into Malaysia they will see that there is no exit stamp in my malaysian passport that says that i departed Australia. Plus upon leaving malaysia i wouldnt want the situation with the check-in lady to be repeated.
And my main concerns for just using my Australian passport for the whole trip is that it will show my city of birth "Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia" and i am nervous that this will cause them to be suspicious and ask questions.
does anyone know what the penalty is for dual citizenship if i get caught out?
can anyone suggest what i can do in this instance? is anyone in the same position and have found some sort of loophole? any advise would be appreciated really.
Thanks :)

Not sure about specifics for Malaysia but the majority of dual citizens of countries where dual citizenship is recognized will use their Australian passport to exit Australia and their other passport to enter the other country.
[User #568854137 postsdyl88Participant] If you want to use both passports then the best way to go is follow this process:
1. Book the tickets under your Malaysian passport
-Travelling to Malaysia 2. Show Malaysian passport at airline check in (OZ) 3. Show Australian passport at leaving immigration (OZ) 4. Show Malaysian passport at arriving immigration (Malaysia)
-Travelling back to Australia 5. Show Australian passport at airline check in (Malaysia) 6. Show Malaysian passport at leaving immigration (Malaysia) 7. Show Australian passport at arriving immigration (Australia)
That's the standard process for travelling on two passports. It's pretty rare for immigration to check stamps now so I don't think you'll run into any problems there. Also obviously keep your Australian passport hidden when you're dealing with Malaysian authorities.

but will the check in person (when im travelling back to Oz) need to check the stamps on my Australian passport that show that i have entered Malaysia though? because if they do then there wont be any. Im not sure if they still use stamps over there.
[User #4681953007 postsThe Old WomanProcrastinating again...Whirlpool Forums Addict] teegoody writes...
but will the check in person (when im travelling back to Oz) need to check the stamps on my Australian passport that show that i have entered Malaysia though?
No. The check in person is only looking for 'do you have the right to enter Australia'. They don't care where you've been.
You would not be showing your Australian passport to any 'officials' in Malaysia.
[User #1299231292 poststheapa? kenapa?Whirlpool Enthusiast] In and out of Malaysia very frequently, on multiple passports.
Australian passport holders automatically get a 90 day visa.
Unless you are planning on staying over 90 days, I would not use the Malaysian passport but you might like wasting heaps of time (and potentially money)at Putrajaya.
[User #936996865 postsvespasienneIn the penalty box] When leaving Australia, Immigration will usually agree to stamp a different passport, if you ask nicely and explain that you may need to show an exit stamp, because *they* (Malaysia in this case) don't permit dual citizenship.
